sections.content: You know *si* + *hubiera* + past participle with *habría* + past participle from B1 Unit 35, and mixed conditionals from B2 Unit 11. In bioethical inquiries and public-health analysis, this pattern is the standard tool for evaluating accountability and past decisions that cannot be undone. In formal writing, *hubiese* alternates freely with *hubiera* as an exact equivalent, and passive *se* clauses keep the focus on institutional responsibility rather than individuals (*Si se hubiese aplicado el protocolo, se habría evitado la negligencia*). When a past ethical failure still shapes the present, the result clause uses the simple conditional (*hoy existiría mayor transparencia*).

sections.title: Counterfactual accountability in formal prose
rows: Past failure -> past consequence (*Si el centro hubiera informado a tiempo, se habría evitado la negligencia.*)
Institutional passive *se* (*Si se hubiese ampliado la inmunización, se habrían reducido los casos.*)
Past failure -> present consequence (*Si hubiera habido más transparencia, hoy habría menos desconfianza.*)

items.spanish: Si el laboratorio hubiera actuado con transparencia, se habría evitado la acusación de negligencia.
items.english: If the laboratory had acted with transparency, the accusation of negligence would have been avoided.

items.spanish: Si se hubiese fortalecido la campaña de inmunización, la salud pública habría sufrido menos presión.
items.english: If the immunisation campaign had been strengthened, public health would have suffered less pressure.

items.spanish: Si el comité hubiese aplicado el principio de beneficencia, hoy no existiría este dilema ético.
items.english: If the committee had applied the principle of beneficence, this ethical dilemma would not exist today.

items.spanish: Si hubieran explicado los riesgos desde el inicio, los pacientes habrían confiado en el equipo.
items.english: If they had explained the risks from the beginning, the patients would have trusted the team.

sections.content: Never place *habría* inside the *si* clause (*Si habría actuado con transparencia* is always wrong). Both *hubiera* and *hubiese* are equally standard in formal Spanish; never treat one as incorrect against the other.
